perspective:
Angela Hwang’s accessible perspective:

- She is Angela, a hairdresser, and has been close friends with Kevin Flores since high school. They often confide in each other. She knows Kevin works as a construction worker and had noticed he seemed unhappy with his job.
- At their coffee meeting, she heard Kevin say he was “alright,” just the usual grind, but then that he was not happy, felt stuck and unfulfilled, and was going through the motions. He told her he had thought about changing jobs/careers but felt overwhelmed and unsure where to start. She offered to figure it out with him; he agreed and thanked her.
- She found job openings and a career counseling service and told Kevin. He thanked her and said he had been thinking about it a lot, and was interested in something more creative, possibly design or architecture. She encouraged him to check the resources; he said he would.
- She believed Kevin was hesitant, so she arranged a meeting with a career coach and told him. He said she didn’t have to, appreciated it, but wasn’t sure he was ready. She encouraged him to try; he agreed to give it a shot. She said she would support him.
- She checked in with Kevin about the career coach. He told her the coach was helpful, he had started online design courses, and he felt more confident. She said she was proud and offered more help. He said her support was enough and he would ask if he needed anything.
- She believed Kevin had successfully transitioned to a new career. She organized a small celebration party and told him. He thanked her, said he was grateful, and said he couldn’t have done it without her. She said he did the hard work and was glad she could support him; they agreed to celebrate.
- Her own feelings/beliefs along the way included concern, support/hope, frustration/worry when he hesitated, pride/relief at his progress, and happiness/satisfaction at his success.
- She does not have access to Kevin’s unspoken/private thoughts or to events she did not observe, hear, or participate in.
